title: Haldiram's Marks Diwali in London With a Chai Rave and Mithai Counter
excerpt: The Leicester Square flagship hosts the Afterglow Chai Rave on November 10 and a Diwali sweet counter selling ladoo, launj and kaju katli.
body:
• Haldiram's is marking Diwali at its Leicester Square restaurant in London with a dedicated counter of traditional Indian sweets.
  • The Afterglow Chai Rave, a post-Diwali party with Coffee Culture, runs on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, from 6 to 8 p.m., with Bollywood, Punjabi, Bhangra and Indo House music.
  • Tickets cost £30 and include snacks, chai and a goodie bag; chai and vada pav will be served.
  • The sweet counter sells mithai including Rose Ladoo, Badam Kesar Launj, Pista Launj and Mango and Strawberry Kaju Katli, to eat in or take home.

Haldiram's is marking Diwali at its Leicester Square restaurant in London with a dedicated counter of traditional Indian sweets and a post-Diwali party, the Afterglow Chai Rave, next Tuesday, according to The Upcoming. The company says the combination aims to bring South Asian food together with London's music and social scene, and to draw a younger crowd.

Plan Your Visit

  • Date: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
  • Time: 6:00–8:00 p.m. GMT
  • Venue: Haldiram's, Leicester Square
  • Address: 19-20 Irving Street, London WC2H 7AU
  • Admission: £30 for the Afterglow Chai Rave, including snacks, chai and a goodie bag
  • Official page: Haldiram's UK

A dancefloor between the mithai counters

The Afterglow Chai Rave is a collaboration with Coffee Culture, a London-based events community that organises culturally themed parties celebrating South Asian music and culture. For two hours, the restaurant will become a dancefloor, with a soundtrack of Bollywood hits, Punjabi music, Bhangra and Indo House. Chai and vada pav — a spiced potato fritter served in a bread roll, a staple of Mumbai street food — will be served during the event.

The Diwali sweet counter

The restaurant has also set up a Diwali sweet counter selling mithai, the traditional Indian sweets commonly exchanged during the festival, to enjoy in the restaurant or take home to share. The counter's range includes Rose Ladoo, Badam Kesar Launj flavoured with saffron and almond, Pista Launj, and Mango and Strawberry Kaju Katli, a fruit-flavoured version of the cashew-based sweet. This year the five-day festival runs from November 6 to 10, with the main day of celebration falling on Sunday, November 8.

According to the team, sharing boxes of mithai at Diwali and meeting friends over street food remain central to the brand's identity, and the Afterglow Chai Rave is an opportunity for those traditions to be taken up by a new generation.

A 1937 Bikaner brand's first UK flagship

Haldiram's was founded in India in 1937 and is best known for its sweets, snacks and savoury dishes. Its Leicester Square site, at 19-20 Irving Street, is described by the company as its first UK flagship, a short walk from Leicester Square station. The brand now has a presence in more than 80 countries.

"While Haldiram's is deeply rooted in tradition, we are equally committed to evolving with our consumers. London is an exciting step in making Haldiram's a household name beyond India."

— Rhea Agarwal, Director of Business Development, Haldiram's UK & EU

For London's Indian diaspora, the format is the story: a festival usually celebrated at home and in community halls is being staged as a ticketed night out in the West End, with the mithai counter doing the traditional work — sweets to gift and share — alongside it.
